claims.claim: The Coast and Geodetic Survey steamer Blake under W. C. Hodgkins worked in Puerto Rico in 1899; at Ponce it measured a 2,572.6-meter base line on the railroad southwest of the city and observed an astronomical azimuth at Cardona Island Lighthouse.
limits: Does not identify South Base by name.
Does not establish that the Ponce base was geodetically identical to any San Juan baseline.

source.publication: Report of the Superintendent, U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey, 1899

claims.claim: During April 1899 Hodgkins's party surveyed the bar and anchorage of San Juan Harbor.
limits: The report characterizes the San Juan work as a harbor survey and does not nominate South Base.
Local survey control may have been established, but that is not demonstrated by this source alone.

source.publication: Report of the Superintendent, U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey, 1899

claims.claim: Stehman Forney led a Coast and Geodetic Survey triangulation party in Puerto Rico from Ponce to San Juan between January and May 1900.
limits: The biographical field-assignment record does not name South Base.
It does not state whether a San Juan station was established, occupied, or reoccupied.

source.publication: Who's Who in the U.S. Coast & Geodetic Survey (1932)

claims.claim: The official NGS Puerto Rico datasheet archive identifies SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE as PID TV1051. Its station history records MONUMENTED by CGS in 1899; the preserved station description is headed 'DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1899 (WCH)' and says the station was marked by a 2-inch iron pipe set vertically in the ground and secured by cement. A 1901 C&GS recovery note records a 20-foot tripod and scaffold signal erected over the station.
limits: The NGS datasheet preserves the substantive historical description but is not the original GA-series field card/image.

The initials WCH are preserved exactly as NGS reports them; expansion to William C. Hodgkins is corroborated by his independently documented command of the 1899 Blake party but is not spelled out in this datasheet.

source.publication: National Geodetic Survey — datasheet PID TV1051 SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE

claims.claim: The same official NGS archive identifies SAN JUAN NORTH BASE as PID TV1049. It also records CGS monumentation in 1899 and a C&GS 1899 description with initials WCH; the mark is likewise described as a 2-inch iron pipe set vertically in the ground and secured by cement.
limits: The paired names and same-year descriptions strongly establish companion controls.

Do not infer that TV1049–TV1051 was a formally measured base line, or substitute their modern adjusted separation for an original measured base length, until a GB/GBZ or equivalent primary record explicitly links them.

source.publication: National Geodetic Survey — datasheet PID TV1049 SAN JUAN NORTH BASE

claims.claim: For TV1051, NGS publishes current survey control at NAD 83(1997) 18°27′07.43134″ N, 66°08′19.12378″ W (third order, adjusted), with SPC PRVI N 268,507.444 m / E 231,128.444 m. It also preserves a superseded Puerto Rico Datum position of 18°27′14.59585″ N, 66°08′20.51227″ W.
limits: NGS explicitly labels the Puerto Rico Datum value superseded and not recommended for current survey control.
Neither the NAD83(1997) adjustment nor the superseded PR value should be relabeled as the original 1899 field coordinate.

source.publication: National Geodetic Survey — datasheet TV1051 SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE

claims.claim: Earlier working hypothesis: South Base may have originated during Forney's 1900 Ponce-to-San Juan triangulation. NGS now records SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051) as MONUMENTED by CGS in 1899 and preserves a C&GS 1899 station description, so 1900 is rejected as the station's initial establishment year. Forney's exact 1900 role remains an occupation/network-integration question.
limits: Do not delete the superseded hypothesis; it documents the earlier research state.
The 1900 campaign remains independently verified, but it is no longer a candidate origin year for the monument.

claims.claim: The magnetic observation point near South Base was distinct from the South Base triangulation station; in 1908 the magnetic station of 1904 was reoccupied between Morro Lighthouse and South Base, 20 paces from South Base, and in 1909 observations were made 50 feet from South Base toward Morro at a separately monumented cement stone.
limits: The magnetic monument is not the South Base triangulation monument.
These records establish relative topology and reuse, not the original establishment date of South Base.

source.publication: Coast and Geodetic Survey Reports, magnetic observations 1908 and 1909

claims.claim: The true bearing from the South Base vicinity to Morro Lighthouse was recorded as N 37°09.4′ E.
limits: Bearing alone does not yield a unique modern coordinate without an authoritative origin and datum transformation.

source.publication: Coast and Geodetic Survey magnetic station descriptions

claims.claim: A reproducible GRS80 inverse-geodesic using official NGS NAD 83(1997) positions for TV1051 SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE and TV1029 MORRO LIGHTHOUSE gives azimuth 37°09′14.97023″ and distance 2,630.119 m. The 1909 C&GS true bearing was 37°09′24.0″; the difference is about 9.03 arcseconds.
limits: This is an independent identity/topology corroboration, not a replacement for the original 1899/1909 reductions.
Historical lighthouse structures changed; the calculation uses the official modern NGS station TV1029 and does not silently equate every lighthouse epoch.

source.publication: Derived from official NGS Data Explorer positions for TV1051 and TV1029; historical comparison from C&GS Report 1909

claims.claim: NOAA hydrographic survey H10076 used a visual signal named MORRO LIGHTHOUSE 1900 and listed the position 18°28′22.774″ N, 66°07′26.371″ W in the Puerto Rico Datum control system of that survey.
limits: The listed position must not be treated as WGS84 without datum transformation.
This supports landmark/control continuity, not South Base identity by itself.

source.publication: NOAA/NOS Hydrographic Survey H10076 descriptive report

claims.claim: A controlled review of 15 nearby NGS records whose archive FIRST_RECV is 1899 found nine stations explicitly classified HISTORY - 1899 FIRST OBSERVED CGS, while SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051) and SAN JUAN NORTH BASE (TV1049) are classified HISTORY - 1899 MONUMENTED CGS. The surviving NGS record therefore distinguishes monumentation from first observation and does not support rewriting TV1051's 1899 monumentation as an 1899 observation.
limits: Absence of a FIRST OBSERVED entry in the NGS datasheet does not prove the station was not observed in 1899.
The first occupation/angle-observation date remains a field-book/GH-series archival question.

source.publication: NGS Puerto Rico control archive and individual datasheets; GALIA 1899-network probe

claims.date_range: 1899 / later adjusted Puerto Rico Datum positions
claims.claim: NGS preserves companion stations SAN JUAN NORTH BASE (TV1049) and SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051), both monumented/described by CGS in 1899. Using their superseded adjusted Puerto Rico Datum positions on Clarke 1866 gives a separation of approximately 1,094.824 m and South-to-North azimuth 6.94493°.
limits: The paired names and geometry do not prove that TV1049–TV1051 was formally measured as a geodetic base line.
Neither NGS datasheet contains explicit BASE LINE, BASELINE, MEASURED BASE, or BASE MEASUREMENT language.
GB/GBZ records remain the controlling source for any formal baseline claim.

source.publication: NGS datasheets TV1049 and TV1051; GALIA read-only base-pair computation

open_gates.target: Recover RG 23 GH horizontal-angle observations, field books, or equivalent records that explicitly date the first occupation/observation of SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051). NGS records 1899 MONUMENTED, not FIRST OBSERVED.

Recover RG 23 GB/GBZ base-measurement or base-line-computation records to determine whether SAN JUAN NORTH BASE (TV1049) and SAN JUAN SOUTH BASE (TV1051) were formally measured as a base line, including length, corrections, date and personnel.
Recover the raw/original 1899 field position/computation and distinguish it from the later superseded adjusted Puerto Rico Datum coordinate retained by NGS.
Recover Forney's 1900 observation/reoccupation records to determine how the already-existing 1899 South Base was used in the Ponce-to-San Juan triangulation.
Recover the original/microfilmed GA-series station-description card/image for TV1051 and TV1049. The substantive station-description text is already recovered from NGS.
